summary: From 31 January to 1 April 2021 an attacker periodically altered Codecov's Bash Uploader script so that it sent the environment variables of customers' CI runs to an outside server. A customer noticed a checksum mismatch and reported it on 1 April.

overview.background: Many CI pipelines download and run Codecov's Bash Uploader to send coverage reports. It runs inside the CI environment where secrets are available as environment variables.
overview.impact: Environment variables in CI, which may include credentials, tokens or keys, and repository remote information were sent out.
overview.severity: Serious supply chain compromise. There were 108 windows of time when the malicious uploader was in use.
overview.gaps: The page does not list how many customers were affected.

diagrams.title: A modified script reads CI secrets
diagrams.caption: Per Codecov, an error in its Docker image creation process let the actor extract a credential and alter the script. The injected line sent the environment to an external IP.

nodes.label: Error in Docker image creation exposes a key
Environment variables sent to external servers

diagrams.title: Verified scripts and short-lived secrets (conceptual)
diagrams.caption: Controls for downloaded CI tools. Codecov also rotated credentials and added monitoring.

timeline.e: Periodic unauthorised alterations of the Bash Uploader begin.
The malicious script runs in customers' CI jobs in 108 windows.
A customer notices the shasum does not match and reports it.
Codecov secures and remediates the script.
Codecov emails affected users and posts the update.
Codecov publishes more detail on exposed variables and customers re-roll credentials.

rootCause.trigger: An attacker obtained a credential through an error in Codecov's Docker image creation process.
rootCause.underlying: The attacker used it to alter the Bash Uploader.
contributing: Customers ran the script without checksum checks
CI secrets were present in the environment
Outbound traffic from CI was not restricted

evidence.label: The unauthorised alteration
evidence.body: beginning January 31, 2021, there were periodic, unauthorized alterations of our Bash Uploader script

evidence.label: The advice
evidence.body: we would suggest you re-roll all of your credentials, tokens, or keys located in the environment variables in your CI process

diagnose.step: Run env in a CI job to list exposed secrets.
Check any stored copy of the uploader for the injected line.
Compare the script's checksum with the published one.

correct.step: Re-roll all credentials in CI environments.
Replace the script with the current version.

verify.step: Check logs for use of exposed tokens.
Check CI no longer contacts unknown IPs.

prevent.step: Verify the checksum before running downloaded scripts.

fix.safety: Rotating secrets can break pipelines. Rotate in a planned order.

troubleshoot.scenario: A coverage tool your CI downloads may have been altered. Your CI jobs hold deploy keys in environment variables.
troubleshoot.question: What do you do?
hints: How do you prevent a repeat?
troubleshoot.answer: List secrets in CI, rotate them, audit their use, pin and verify downloaded tools, and restrict egress.

options: A customer saw a shasum mismatch

design.prompt: Design CI that cannot leak secrets through a tool.
design.answer: OIDC short-lived credentials, isolated steps, egress allowlist and verified tools.
